newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end higher, led by bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end higher, led by bargain hunting.

text.p: Shares ended Wednesday's trading in positive territory, boosted by bargain hunting after recent sharp falls, brokers said.
They added that sentiment was briefly brightened by the parliamentary ratification of South Korea's entry in the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development.
Easing of worries about the exchange's new trading system and expanded trading range also boosted sentiment, they said.
The composite stock index rose 6.65 points to a provisional close of 722.62. Advancers beat decliners 715 to 184. Despite the climb, volume was a thin 19.9 million shares.

Traders began using a new computer system from Monday. The share trading range was also expanded at the beginning of the week to eight percent up or down from the previous days close, up from the previous six percent.

"This was basically a technical rebound," said an LG Securities broker. "I don't think the market advance will continue into next week. Market interest rates are above 12 percent, there's an imbalance between supply and demand, and the sale of Korea Telecom shares will further depress sentiment."
The finance ministry will sell 360 billion won worth of unlisted Korea Telecom shares on Thursday and Friday.
He saw support for the market at the 700 point level.
Jay Kwon of Hanwha Securities was a little more optimistic.
"I think the market will move sideways at around the 720 level for the time being," Kwon said.

Customer deposits, at around 2.4 trillion won, are lagging behind loans out for margin trading, which are valued at 2.8 trillion. Brokers estimate that 800 billion won in margin loans will have to be paid back in early December.
KEPCO was actively bought by foreigners, rising 100 won to 26,000.
